title.en: Volume 175 Biographies 125: Xianzong's Ten Sons, Muzong's Five Sons, Jingzong's Five Sons, Wenzong's Two Sons, Wuzong's Five Sons, Xuanzong's Ten Sons, Xizong's Eight Sons, Xizong's Two Sons, Zhaozong's Ten Sons
title.raw: 卷一百七十五 列傳第一百二十五: 憲宗二十子 穆宗五子 敬宗五子 文宗二子 武宗五子 宣宗十一子 懿宗八子 僖宗二子 昭宗十子 Volume 175 Biographies 125: Xianzong's Ten Sons, Muzong's Five Sons, Jingzong's Five Sons, Wenzong's Two Sons, Wuzong's Five Sons, Xuanzong's Ten Sons, Xizong's Eight Sons, Xizong's Two Sons, Zhaozong's Ten Sons

sentences.zh: 憲宗二十子：穆宗皇帝、宣宗皇帝、惠昭太子寧、澧王惲、深王悰、洋王忻、絳王悟、建王恪、鄜王憬、瓊王悅、沔王恂、婺王懌、茂王愔、淄王協、衡王憺、澶王㤝、棣王惴、彭王惕、信王憻、榮王㥽。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong had twenty sons: Emperor Muzong, Emperor Xuanzong, Heir Apparent Huizhao Ning, Prince of Li Yun, Prince of Shen Cong, Prince of Yang Xin, Prince of Jiang Wu, Prince of Jian Ke, Prince of Zheng Jing, Prince of Qiong Yue, Prince of Mian Xiong, Prince of Wu Yi, Prince of Mao Yin, Prince of Zi Xie, Prince of Heng Dan, Prince of Chan Huang, Prince of Di Zhui, Prince of Peng Ti, Prince of Xin Tan, Prince of Rong Le.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong had twenty sons: the emperors Muzong and Xuanzong; Heir Apparent Huizhao, Ning; and the princes of Li (Yun), Shen (Cong), Yang (Xin), Jiang (Wu), Jian (Ke), Zheng (Jing), Qiong (Yue), Mian (Xiong), Wu (Yi), Mao (Yin), Zi (Xie), Heng (Dan), Chan (Huang), Di (Zhui), Peng (Ti), Xin (Tan), and Rong (Le).

sentences.zh: 惠昭太子寧，憲宗長子也。

translations.literal: Heir Apparent Huizhao Ning was Emperor Xianzong's eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Heir Apparent Huizhao, Ning, was Emperor Xianzong's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 母曰紀美人。

translations.literal: His mother was the Beautiful Lady Ji.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was Lady Ji, a palace beauty.

sentences.zh: 貞元二十一年四月，封平原郡王。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the twenty-first year of Zhenyuan, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Pingyuan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In April of 805, he was created Prince of Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 元和元年八月，進封鄧王。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Yuanhe, he was advanced to Prince of Deng.
translations.idiomatic: In August of 806, he was promoted to Prince of Deng.

sentences.zh: 四年閏三月，立為皇太子，改名宙，尋復今名。

translations.literal: In the intercalary third month of the fourth year, he was installed as crown prince, his name was changed to Zhou, and soon afterward restored to his present name.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary third month of 809, he was made crown prince; his name was briefly changed to Zhou, then soon restored to Ning.

sentences.zh: 其年有司將行冊禮，以孟夏、孟秋再卜日，臨事皆以雨罷，至十月方行冊禮。

translations.literal: That year the responsible offices were to perform the investiture rites; they divined dates twice, in early summer and early autumn, but each time rain caused cancellation when the ceremony was at hand, and only in the tenth month were the investiture rites carried out.
translations.idiomatic: That year the authorities prepared to conduct the formal investiture, but divinations for dates in early summer and early autumn were each called off when rain fell on the appointed days; the rites were not performed until the tenth month.

sentences.zh: 元和六年十二月薨，年十九，廢朝十三日。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the sixth year of Yuanhe he died, aged nineteen; court audiences were suspended for thirteen days.
translations.idiomatic: He died in December 811, at the age of nineteen, and court was suspended for thirteen days.

sentences.zh: 時敕國子司業裴茝攝太常博士，西內勾當。

translations.literal: At the time an edict ordered Pei Chang, Vice Director of the Directorate of Education, to act as Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and to manage affairs within the Western Inner Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered Pei Chang, vice director of the Imperial University, to serve concurrently as a ritual specialist of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and to oversee arrangements within the western inner palace.

sentences.zh: 茝通習古今禮儀，嘗為太常博士。

translations.literal: Chang was thoroughly versed in ancient and modern ritual, and had once served as Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Chang was thoroughly versed in ritual practice past and present and had previously held the post of ritual erudite in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 及官至郎中，每兼其職，至改司業，方罷兼領。

translations.literal: When he reached the rank of Director, he always held that office concurrently; only when he was transferred to Vice Director did he cease the concurrent appointment.
translations.idiomatic: After he rose to director in the Ministry of Rites, he continued to hold the ritual post on a concurrent basis until his appointment as vice director of the Imperial University, when he finally relinquished it.

sentences.zh: 國典無皇太子薨禮，故又命茝領之。

translations.literal: The state regulations had no rites for the death of a crown prince, so he was again ordered to take charge of them.
translations.idiomatic: Because the state code prescribed no funeral rites for a deceased crown prince, Chang was again put in charge of the ceremony.

sentences.zh: 廢朝十三日，蓋用期服以日易月之制也。

translations.literal: The suspension of court for thirteen days was presumably applying the regulation for one-year mourning in which days stand in for months.
translations.idiomatic: The thirteen-day suspension of court presumably followed the rule for one-year mourning, counting each day as a month.

sentences.zh: 謚曰惠昭。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Huizhao.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title Huizhao, meaning Benevolent and Illustrious.

sentences.zh: 澧王惲，憲宗第二子也，本名寬。

translations.literal: Prince of Li Yun was Emperor Xianzong's second son; his original name was Kuan.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Li, Yun, was Emperor Xianzong's second son; his original name was Kuan.

sentences.zh: 貞元二十一年，封同安郡王。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Zhenyuan he was enfeoffed as Prince of Tong'an commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In 805 he was created Prince of Tong'an.

sentences.zh: 元和元年，進封澧王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanhe he was advanced to Prince of Li.
translations.idiomatic: In 806 he was promoted to Prince of Li.

sentences.zh: 七年，改今名。

translations.literal: In the seventh year his present name was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: In 812 he received his present name, Yun.

sentences.zh: 時吐突承璀恩寵特異，惠昭太子薨，議立儲副，承璀獨排群議，屬澧王，欲以威權自樹，賴憲宗明斷不惑。

translations.literal: At that time Tutu Chenghui enjoyed exceptional favor; when Heir Apparent Huizhao died and the succession was debated, Chenghui alone rejected the collective opinion and backed the Prince of Li, seeking to build his own authority through power, but thanks to Emperor Xianzong's clear judgment he was not misled.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the eunuch Tutu Chenghui enjoyed extraordinary favor. After Heir Apparent Huizhao's death, when the court debated who should be named heir, Chenghui alone defied the consensus and backed the Prince of Li, hoping to build his own power base; only Emperor Xianzong's clear judgment kept him from being swayed.

sentences.zh: 上將冊拜太子，詔翰林學士崔群代澧王作讓表一章。

translations.literal: When the emperor was about to invest the crown prince, he ordered Hanlin Academician Cui Qun to draft on the Prince of Li's behalf a chapter of declination memorial.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was about to invest the new crown prince, he ordered the Hanlin academician Cui Qun to draft, on behalf of the Prince of Li, a memorial declining the appointment.

sentences.zh: 群奏曰：「凡事己合當之而不為，則有退讓焉。

translations.literal: Qun submitted: 'In all matters, when one ought to receive something and does not, there is declination.'
translations.idiomatic: Cui Qun submitted: "In any matter, declination applies only when one who ought to receive an honor refuses it."

sentences.zh: 」上深納之。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted this view wholeheartedly.

sentences.zh: 及憲宗晏駕，承璀死，王亦薨於其夕。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianzong passed away, Chenghui died, and the prince also died that same evening.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianzong died, Chenghui died as well, and the prince died that same night.

sentences.zh: 以元和十五年四月丁丑發喪，廢朝三日。

translations.literal: Funeral observances began on the dingchou day of the fourth month of the fifteenth year of Yuanhe; court was suspended for three days.
translations.idiomatic: Funeral rites began on a dingchou day in April 820, and court was suspended for three days.

sentences.zh: 長子漢，東陽郡王。

translations.literal: His eldest son Han was Prince of Dongyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son, Han, was Prince of Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 次子源，安陸郡王。

translations.literal: His second son Yuan was Prince of Anlu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His second son, Yuan, was Prince of Anlu.

sentences.zh: 第三子演，臨安郡王。

translations.literal: His third son Yan was Prince of Lin'an commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His third son, Yan, was Prince of Lin'an.

sentences.zh: 深王悰，本名察，憲宗第四子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Shen Cong; his original name was Cha; he was Emperor Xianzong's fourth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Shen, Cong, whose original name was Cha, was Emperor Xianzong's fourth son.

sentences.zh: 貞元二十一年，封彭城郡王。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Zhenyuan he was enfeoffed as Prince of Pengcheng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In 805 he was created Prince of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 元和元年，進封深王，改今名。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanhe he was advanced to Prince of Shen and given his present name.
translations.idiomatic: In 806 he was promoted to Prince of Shen and received his present name.

sentences.zh: 長子潭，河內郡王。

translations.literal: His eldest son Tan was Prince of Henei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son, Tan, was Prince of Henei.

sentences.zh: 次子淑，吳興郡王。

translations.literal: His second son Shu was Prince of Wuxing commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His second son, Shu, was Prince of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 洋王忻，本名寰，憲宗第五子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Yang Xin; his original name was Huan; he was Emperor Xianzong's fifth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Yang, Xin, whose original name was Huan, was Emperor Xianzong's fifth son.

sentences.zh: 貞元二十一年，封為高密郡王。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Zhenyuan he was enfeoffed as Prince of Gaomi commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In 805 he was created Prince of Gaomi.

sentences.zh: 元和元年，進封洋王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanhe he was advanced to Prince of Yang.
translations.idiomatic: In 806 he was promoted to Prince of Yang.

sentences.zh: 七年，改今名。

translations.literal: In the seventh year his present name was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: In 812 he received his present name.

sentences.zh: 太和二年薨。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taihe he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 828.

sentences.zh: 長子沛，太和八年，封潁川郡王。

translations.literal: His eldest son Pei, in the eighth year of Taihe, was enfeoffed as Prince of Yingchuan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son, Pei, was created Prince of Yingchuan in 834.

sentences.zh: 絳王悟，本名寮，憲宗第六子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Jiang Wu; his original name was Liao; he was Emperor Xianzong's sixth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jiang, Wu, whose original name was Liao, was Emperor Xianzong's sixth son.

sentences.zh: 貞元二十一年，封文安郡王。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Zhenyuan he was enfeoffed as Prince of Wen'an commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In 805 he was created Prince of Wen'an.

sentences.zh: 元和元年，進封絳王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanhe he was advanced to Prince of Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: In 806 he was promoted to Prince of Jiang.

sentences.zh: 七年，改今名。

translations.literal: In the seventh year his present name was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: In 812 he received his present name.

sentences.zh: 寶歷二年冬遇害。

translations.literal: In the winter of the second year of Baoli he was murdered.
translations.idiomatic: He was murdered in the winter of 826.

sentences.zh: 長子洙，太和八年，封新安郡王。

translations.literal: His eldest son Zhu, in the eighth year of Taihe, was enfeoffed as Prince of Xin'an commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son, Zhu, was created Prince of Xin'an in 834.

sentences.zh: 第二子滂，封高平郡王。

translations.literal: His second son Pang was enfeoffed as Prince of Gaoping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His second son, Pang, was created Prince of Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 建王恪，本名審，憲宗第十子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Jian Ke; his original name was Shen; he was Emperor Xianzong's tenth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jian, Ke, whose original name was Shen, was Emperor Xianzong's tenth son.

sentences.zh: 元和元年八月，淄青節度李師古卒，其弟師道擅領軍務，以邀符節。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Yuanhe, Ziqing military commissioner Li Shigu died; his younger brother Shidao seized control of military affairs on his own authority to demand the commissioner's seal and baton.
translations.idiomatic: In August 806, Li Shigu, military commissioner of Ziqing, died; his younger brother Shidao seized command of the army on his own authority in hopes of securing the commission.

sentences.zh: 朝廷方興討罰之師，不欲分兵兩地，乃封審為建王。

translations.literal: The court was just then raising punitive troops and did not wish to divide forces between two regions, so Shen was enfeoffed as Prince of Jian.
translations.idiomatic: The court was already mobilizing troops to punish the rebels and did not wish to divide its forces, so it enfeoffed Shen as Prince of Jian instead.

sentences.zh: 間一日，授開府儀同三司、鄆州大都督，充平盧軍淄青等州節度營田觀察處置、陸運海運、押新羅渤海兩蕃等使，而以師道為節度留後。

translations.literal: The next day he was appointed Grand Preceptor of the Palace with the same ceremonial honors as the Three Excellencies, Grand Protector-General of Yanzhou, and Commissioner for the Pinglu Army, Ziqing and other circuits' military, farming, and inspection affairs, land and sea transport, and supervision of the two foreign states Silla and Bohai, while Shidao was made acting military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The following day he was appointed Grand Preceptor with ceremonial honors equal to the Three Excellencies and Grand Protector-General of Yanzhou, and named commissioner over the Pinglu and Ziqing circuits' military, farming, and inspection affairs, over land and sea transport, and over relations with Silla and Bohai—while Shidao was left as acting military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 不出閣。

translations.literal: He did not leave the palace residence.
translations.idiomatic: He never actually left the capital to take up his post.

sentences.zh: 七年，改今名。

translations.literal: In the seventh year his present name was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: In 812 he received his present name.

sentences.zh: 長慶元年薨。

translations.literal: In the first year of Changqing he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 821.

sentences.zh: 鄜王憬，長慶元年封，開成四年七月薨。

translations.literal: Prince of Zheng Jing was enfeoffed in the first year of Changqing and died in the seventh month of the fourth year of Kaicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Zheng, Jing, was enfeoffed in 821 and died in July 839.

sentences.zh: 長子溥，平陽郡王。

translations.literal: His eldest son Pu was Prince of Pingyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son, Pu, was Prince of Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 瓊王悅，長慶元年封。

translations.literal: Prince of Qiong Yue was enfeoffed in the first year of Changqing.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Qiong, Yue, was enfeoffed in 821.

sentences.zh: 第二子津，河間郡王。

translations.literal: His second son Jin was Prince of Hejian commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His second son, Jin, was Prince of Hejian.

sentences.zh: 婺王懌，長慶元年封。

translations.literal: Prince of Wu Yi was enfeoffed in the first year of Changqing.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Wu, Yi, was enfeoffed in 821.

sentences.zh: 長子清，新平郡王。

translations.literal: His eldest son Qing was Prince of Xinping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son, Qing, was Prince of Xinping.

sentences.zh: 茂王愔，長慶元年封。

translations.literal: Prince of Mao Yin was enfeoffed in the first year of Changqing.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Mao, Yin, was enfeoffed in 821.

sentences.zh: 長子潓，武功郡王。

translations.literal: His eldest son Wei was Prince of Wugong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son, Wei, was Prince of Wugong.

sentences.zh: 淄王協，憲宗第十四子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Zi Xie was Emperor Xianzong's fourteenth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Zi, Xie, was Emperor Xianzong's fourteenth son.

sentences.zh: 長慶元年封，開成元年薨。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed in the first year of Changqing and died in the first year of Kaicheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed in 821 and died in 836.

sentences.zh: 長子浣，太和八年八月封許昌郡王。

translations.literal: His eldest son Huan, in the eighth month of the eighth year of Taihe, was enfeoffed as Prince of Xuchang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son, Huan, was created Prince of Xuchang in August 834.

sentences.zh: 第三子渙，馮翊郡王。

translations.literal: His third son Huan was Prince of Fengyi commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His third son, Huan, was Prince of Fengyi.

sentences.zh: 澶王㤝，長慶元年封。

translations.literal: Prince of Chan Huang was enfeoffed in the first year of Changqing.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Chan, Huang, was enfeoffed in 821.

sentences.zh: 長子濘，雁門郡王。

translations.literal: His eldest son Ning was Prince of Yanmen commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son, Ning, was Prince of Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 棣王惴，大中六年封，咸通三年薨。

translations.literal: Prince of Di Zhui was enfeoffed in the sixth year of Dazhong and died in the third year of Xiantong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Di, Zhui, was enfeoffed in 852 and died in 862.

sentences.zh: 彭王惕，大中三年封。

translations.literal: Prince of Peng Ti was enfeoffed in the third year of Dazhong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Peng, Ti, was enfeoffed in 849.

sentences.zh: 信王憻，大中十四年封，咸通八年薨。

translations.literal: Prince of Xin Tan was enfeoffed in the fourteenth year of Dazhong and died in the eighth year of Xiantong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Xin, Tan, was enfeoffed in 860 and died in 867.

sentences.zh: 榮王㥽，咸通三年封，廣明元年八月十九日，授開府儀同三司，守司空，其年十月九日薨。

translations.literal: Prince of Rong Le was enfeoffed in the third year of Xiantong; on the nineteenth day of the eighth month of the first year of Guangming he was appointed Grand Preceptor with ceremonial honors equal to the Three Excellencies and Acting Minister of Works; he died on the ninth day of the tenth month of that year.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Rong, Le, was enfeoffed in 862. On the nineteenth day of the eighth month of 880 he was appointed Grand Preceptor with honors equal to the Three Excellencies and acting Minister of Works; he died on the ninth day of the tenth month of that year.

sentences.zh: 其子令平嗣王。

translations.literal: His son Lingping succeeded to the princedom.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lingping succeeded him as prince.

sentences.zh: 穆宗五子：敬宗皇帝、文宗皇帝、武宗皇帝、懷懿太子湊、安王溶。

translations.literal: Emperor Muzong had five sons: Emperor Jingzong, Emperor Wenzong, Emperor Wuzong, Heir Apparent Huaiyi Cou, and Prince of An Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Muzong had five sons: the emperors Jingzong, Wenzong, and Wuzong; Heir Apparent Huaiyi, Cou; and Prince of An, Rong.

sentences.zh: 懷懿太子湊，穆宗第六子。

translations.literal: Heir Apparent Huaiyi Cou was Emperor Muzong's sixth son.
translations.idiomatic: Heir Apparent Huaiyi, Cou, was Emperor Muzong's sixth son.

sentences.zh: 少寬和溫雅，齊莊有度。

translations.literal: From youth he was generous, gentle, warm, and refined, dignified and measured in deportment.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he was generous, gentle, and refined, dignified and measured in his bearing.

sentences.zh: 長慶初，封漳王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Changqing he was enfeoffed as Prince of Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Changqing era (821–824), he was created Prince of Zhang.

sentences.zh: 文宗以王守澄恃權，深怒閹官，欲盡誅之，密令宰相宋申錫與外臣謀畫其計。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong, because Wang Shoucheng relied on his power, deeply hated the eunuchs and wished to execute them all; he secretly ordered Chancellor Song Shenxi and outer-court officials to devise a plan.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong deeply resented the eunuchs' monopoly of power, especially Wang Shoucheng, and wished to eliminate them entirely; he secretly ordered Chancellor Song Shenxi and officials outside the palace to devise a plan.

sentences.zh: 守澄門人鄭註伺知其事，欲先事誅申錫。

translations.literal: Shoucheng's follower Zheng Zhu learned of the affair by spying and wished to kill Shenxi first.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Zhu, a protégé of Shoucheng, discovered the plot through surveillance and resolved to strike first by eliminating Shenxi.

sentences.zh: 以漳王賢而有望，乃令神策虞候豆盧著告變言：「十六宅宮市典宴敬則、硃訓與申錫親吏王師文同謀不軌，硃訓與王師文言聖上多病，太子年小，若立兄弟，次是漳王，要先結托，乃於師文處得銀五鋌、絹八百匹；

translations.literal: Because the Prince of Zhang was worthy and held promise, he had the Shence Army duty officer Dou Lu Zhu report a treasonous plot, saying: 'The Sixteen Mansions palace market steward Yan Jingze and Zhu Xun, together with Shenxi's intimate clerk Wang Shiwen, plotted sedition; Zhu Xun and Wang Shiwen said the Son of Heaven was often ill and the crown prince young; if an elder brother were to be established, the Prince of Zhang would be next in line, and they must first secure his support—thus from Shiwen they obtained five ingots of silver and eight hundred bolts of silk;'
translations.idiomatic: Because the Prince of Zhang was talented and widely regarded as a possible heir, Zhu had the Shence Army duty officer Dou Lu Zhu lodge a treason report: "Yan Jingze, steward of the palace market at the Sixteen Mansions, and Zhu Xun, together with Song Shenxi's personal clerk Wang Shiwen, plotted sedition. Zhu Xun and Wang Shiwen said that since the emperor was often ill and the crown prince still young, if an elder brother were to be enthroned the Prince of Zhang would be next in line, and they must secure his backing first—they had obtained from Shiwen five silver ingots and eight hundred bolts of silk;"

sentences.zh: 又晏敬則於十六宅將出漳王吳綾汗衫一領、熟線綾一匹，以答申錫。

translations.literal: furthermore Yan Jingze was to take from the Sixteen Mansions one sweat-shirt of Wu brocade and one bolt of finished-thread brocade belonging to the Prince of Zhang, to present to Shenxi in return.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Jingze was also to take from the prince's residence at the Sixteen Mansions one sweat-shirt of Wu brocade and one bolt of finished-thread brocade to present to Shenxi in return.

sentences.zh: 」其事皆鄭註憑虛結構，而擒硃訓等於黃門獄，鍛煉偽成其款。

translations.literal: The entire affair was fabricated out of nothing by Zheng Zhu; Zhu Xun and the others were seized in the Yellow Gate prison, and false confessions were forged through torture.
translations.idiomatic: The entire affair was fabricated by Zheng Zhu out of thin air. Zhu Xun and the others were seized and held in the eunuchs' prison, where tortured confessions were forged to fit the fabricated charges.

sentences.zh: 居三四日，朝臣方悟其誣構。

translations.literal: After three or four days the court officials finally realized it was a fabricated frame-up.
translations.idiomatic: Only after three or four days did the court officials realize the case was a fabrication.

sentences.zh: 諫官崔玄亮等閣中極諫，叩頭出血，請出申錫獄付外勘鞫。

translations.literal: Remonstrance officials including Cui Xuanliang remonstrated vehemently at the palace gate, knocking their heads until they bled, requesting that Shenxi be removed from prison and handed over to the outer court for investigation and trial.
translations.idiomatic: The remonstrance officials Cui Xuanliang and others pleaded desperately at the palace gate, knocking their foreheads until they bled, begging that Shenxi be removed from the eunuchs' custody and transferred to the regular courts for investigation.

sentences.zh: 鄭註輩恐其偽跡敗露，乃請行貶黜。

translations.literal: Zheng Zhu and his faction, fearing their fabrications would be exposed, then requested that demotions be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Zhu and his allies, fearing their fabrications would be exposed, pressed instead for immediate demotions.

sentences.zh: 制曰：「王者教先入愛，義不遺親。

translations.literal: An edict stated: 'A king's teaching enters first through love; in righteousness he does not abandon his kin.'
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "A ruler's teaching must begin with affection; righteousness does not permit him to abandon his own kin."

sentences.zh: 豈於同氣之中，可致異詞之間。

translations.literal: How among those of the same vital breath could one bring about words of estrangement.
translations.idiomatic: How could words of estrangement arise among those who share the same blood?

sentences.zh: 如或慎修不至，詿誤有聞，構為厲階，犯我邦紀，未加殛竄，尚屈彜章。

translations.literal: If through insufficient careful cultivation errors were heard of, and a perilous step was constructed violating our state's regulations, execution and banishment were not yet applied, but still the regular statutes were bent.
translations.idiomatic: If through want of careful conduct errors come to light, and a perilous course is plotted in violation of the state's laws, execution and banishment might be warranted—yet even then the regular statutes may be tempered.

sentences.zh: 漳王湊手足之親，盤石是固，居崇寵秩，列在戚籓。

translations.literal: The Prince of Zhang Cou is kin of hand and foot, solid as bedrock, dwelling in honored favor and rank, listed among the imperial affines.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Zhang, Cou, is the emperor's own brother, firm as bedrock, dwelling in honored rank among the imperial princes.

sentences.zh: 頃多克順之心，亦有尚賢之誌。

translations.literal: Recently he has shown much a heart of self-restraint and compliance, and also an ambition to honor the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: He has long shown a disposition toward restraint and compliance, and an ambition to honor worthy men.

sentences.zh: 而滿盈生患，敗覆是圖，奸兇會同，謀議聯及。

translations.literal: Yet fullness and excess breed calamity; ruin and overthrow were plotted; treacherous villains joined together and the conspiracy extended in linked counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Yet fullness breeds calamity, and ruin was plotted; treacherous villains joined together in a linked conspiracy.

sentences.zh: 汙我皇化，彰於外朝，初駭予衷，再驚群聽。

translations.literal: They defiled our imperial transformation, making it manifest in the outer court; at first it startled my heart, and again it alarmed all who heard.
translations.idiomatic: They have defiled the imperial order and made their plot known throughout the outer court—at first shocking my own heart, and then alarming all who heard.

sentences.zh: 尚以未具獄詞，猶資審慎，建侯之命，姑務從寬。

translations.literal: Still, because the prison testimony was not yet complete, caution was still exercised; the command to establish a feudatory lord was for the time being treated with leniency.
translations.idiomatic: Because the case has not yet been fully established, caution is still required; the command to enfeoff a prince will for the present be tempered with leniency.

sentences.zh: 可降封巢縣公。

translations.literal: He may be demoted and enfeoffed as Duke of Chaoxian.
translations.idiomatic: He is demoted and created Duke of Chaoxian.

sentences.zh: 」制下，上令中使賫巢縣官告，就十宅賜湊。

translations.literal: When the edict was issued, the emperor ordered a palace envoy to carry the Chaoxian commission patent and bestow it on Cou at the Ten Mansions.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict was issued, the emperor sent a palace envoy bearing the patent of appointment as Duke of Chaoxian to Cou's residence at the Ten Mansions.

sentences.zh: 言國法須此，爾宜寬勉。

translations.literal: He said state law required this, and you should take comfort and encourage yourself.
translations.idiomatic: He told Cou that state law required this measure and urged him to take comfort and persevere.

sentences.zh: 八年薨，贈封齊王。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he died; posthumously he was enfeoffed as Prince of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 833 and was posthumously created Prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 鄭註伏誅。

translations.literal: Zheng Zhu was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Zhu was executed.

sentences.zh: 帝思湊被陷而心傷之，開成三年正月制曰：

translations.literal: The emperor, thinking of Cou's having been framed, was grieved at heart; in the first month of the third year of Kaicheng an edict stated:
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, grieving that Cou had been framed, issued an edict in the first month of 838:

sentences.zh: 褒善飾終，王者常典。

translations.literal: Commending goodness and adorning the end—this is the constant norm of kings.
translations.idiomatic: To commend the virtuous and honor the dead is the constant duty of a ruler.

sentences.zh: 況我友於之愛，手足之親，永言痛悼之懷，用錫元良之命。

translations.literal: How much more for the love between friends, the kinship of hand and foot—ever speaking the feeling of painful mourning, bestowing the command of the primary worthy.
translations.idiomatic: How much more when the bond is that of brothers, kin of hand and foot—in lasting grief I now bestow the title of primary heir.

sentences.zh: 故齊王湊孕靈天宇，擢秀本枝，孝敬知於孩提，惠和洽於親愛。

translations.literal: The late Prince of Qi Cou received his spirit from Heaven and Earth, was selected as excellence from the main branch, filial respect known from infancy, kindness and harmony reaching his kin.
translations.idiomatic: The late Prince of Qi, Cou, received his spirit from Heaven and Earth and stood out among the imperial sons; filial devotion was evident from his earliest years, and kindness and harmony marked his relations with kin.

sentences.zh: 將固磐石，遂分茅社。

translations.literal: About to make bedrock firm, he then received fief and altars.
translations.idiomatic: He was on the verge of securing the realm as bedrock, and was accordingly granted a princely fief.

sentences.zh: 學探蟻術之精，智有象舟之妙。

translations.literal: In study he probed the refinement of ant-craft skill; in wisdom he possessed the subtlety of elephant-boat craft.
translations.idiomatic: In scholarship he pursued the finest refinements; in wisdom he showed exceptional subtlety.

sentences.zh: 好書樂善，造次不失其清規；

translations.literal: He loved books and delighted in goodness; even in haste he did not depart from his pure standards.
translations.idiomatic: He loved books and delighted in goodness, never departing from proper conduct even in haste.

sentences.zh: 置醴尊師，風雨不忘其至敬。

translations.literal: He set out libations and honored teachers; in wind and rain he did not forget his utmost reverence.
translations.idiomatic: He set out libations to honor his teachers and never failed in his utmost reverence, even in wind and rain.

sentences.zh: 方期臺耇，以保怡怡，天胡不仁，殲我同氣。

translations.literal: Just when he might have reached the terrace of longevity to preserve harmonious kinship, how could Heaven be so unkind as to destroy my brother of the same breath?
translations.idiomatic: Just when he might have reached a long life to preserve harmonious kinship, how could Heaven be so unkind as to destroy my own brother?

sentences.zh: 念周宣好愛之分，長慟莫追；

translations.literal: Recalling King Xuan of Zhou's affectionate regard, I grieve long with nothing to pursue.
translations.idiomatic: Recalling King Xuan of Zhou's affection for his kin, I grieve endlessly with nothing to restore.

sentences.zh: 覽魏文榮樂之言，軫懷無已。

translations.literal: Reading Emperor Wen of Wei's words on glory and joy, my sorrowing heart knows no end.
translations.idiomatic: Reading Emperor Wen of Wei's words on glory and joy, my grieving heart knows no end.

sentences.zh: 由是稽諸前典，式殿追榮，特峻彜章，表恩泉壞。

translations.literal: Therefore I examined the former canons and modeled the hall of posthumous honor, especially elevating the regular statutes to display grace at the spring mound.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly I consulted the former canons and modeled posthumous honors, especially elevating his rank to display grace at his tomb.

sentences.zh: 雖禮命之儀則爾，而天倫之恨何攄？

translations.literal: Although the ritual command follows its rules, how can the hatred of natural kinship be dispelled?
translations.idiomatic: Although ritual propriety must be observed, how can the grief of natural kinship be dispelled?

sentences.zh: 遐想幽魂，宜膺寵數。

translations.literal: Contemplating the remote soul, he should receive favored honors.
translations.idiomatic: Contemplating his departed soul, he should receive favored honors.

sentences.zh: 可贈懷懿太子，有司擇日冊命。

translations.literal: He may be posthumously granted Heir Apparent Huaiyi; the responsible offices shall choose a day for the investiture.
translations.idiomatic: He is posthumously granted the title Heir Apparent Huaiyi; the responsible offices shall choose a day for the investiture.

sentences.zh: 安王溶，穆宗第八子。

translations.literal: Prince of An Rong was Emperor Muzong's eighth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of An, Rong, was Emperor Muzong's eighth son.

sentences.zh: 母楊賢妃，長慶元年封。

translations.literal: His mother was the Worthy Consort Yang; in the first year of Changqing he was enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was Worthy Consort Yang; he was enfeoffed in 821.

sentences.zh: 太和八年，授開府儀同三司、檢校吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Taihe he was appointed Grand Preceptor with ceremonial honors equal to the Three Excellencies and Acting Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In 834 he was appointed Grand Preceptor with honors equal to the Three Excellencies and acting Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 開成初，敕安王、潁王，並以百官例，逐月給料錢。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaicheng an edict ordered the Princes of An and Ying to receive monthly salary payments according to the standard for officials.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Kaicheng era, an edict ordered the Princes of An and Ying to receive monthly salary payments on the same terms as officials.

sentences.zh: 武宗即位，李德裕秉政，或告文宗崩時，楊嗣復以與賢妃宗家，欲立安王為嗣，故王受禍，嗣復貶官。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wuzong took the throne, Li Deyu held power; some reported that when Emperor Wenzong died, Yang Sifu, being of the same clan as the Worthy Consort, wished to establish the Prince of An as successor, so the prince suffered disaster and Sifu was demoted.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wuzong took the throne, Li Deyu held power; some reported that at Emperor Wenzong's death Yang Sifu, being related to Worthy Consort Yang's clan, had wished to establish the Prince of An as heir, and for this the prince suffered and Sifu was demoted.

sentences.zh: 敬宗五子：悼懷太子普、梁王休復、襄王執中、紀王言揚、陳王成美。

translations.literal: Emperor Jingzong had five sons: Heir Apparent Daohuai Pu, Prince of Liang Xiufu, Prince of Xiang Zhizhong, Prince of Ji Yanyang, and Prince of Chen Chengmei.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jingzong had five sons: Heir Apparent Daohuai, Pu; and the princes of Liang (Xiufu), Xiang (Zhizhong), Ji (Yanyang), and Chen (Chengmei).

sentences.zh: 梁王休復。

translations.literal: Prince of Liang Xiufu.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Liang, Xiufu.

sentences.zh: 開成二年八月詔曰：「王者胙土畫疆，封建子弟，所以承衛帝室，蕃茂本枝，祖宗成式，朕曷敢廢？

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the second year of Kaicheng an edict stated: A king who grants fief and draws boundaries enfeoffs sons and younger brothers in order to guard the imperial house and make the main branch flourish; this is the established pattern of the ancestors—how dare I abolish it?
translations.idiomatic: In August 837 an edict declared: A ruler who grants fief and draws boundaries enfeoffs his sons and younger brothers to guard the imperial house and strengthen the main branch; this is the established pattern of our ancestors—how dare I abolish it?

sentences.zh: 況天付正性，夙奉至訓，尊賢好善，體仁由禮，是可舉建侯之命，膺分社之榮。

translations.literal: How much more when Heaven bestowed a correct nature and from youth he received the utmost instruction, honoring the worthy and loving goodness, embodying benevolence through ritual—he may receive the command to establish a feudatory lord and bear the glory of sharing the altars.
translations.idiomatic: How much more when Heaven bestowed a correct nature and from youth he received the utmost instruction, honoring the worthy, loving goodness, and embodying benevolence through ritual—he is fit to receive the command to establish a feudatory lord and share in the glory of the altars.

sentences.zh: 親親賢賢，於是乎在。

translations.literal: Cherishing kin and honoring the worthy—therein lies the principle.
translations.idiomatic: Cherishing kin and honoring the worthy—that is the principle.

sentences.zh: 敬宗皇帝第二子休復、第三子執中、第四子言揚、第六子成美，皆氣蘊中和，行推敬慎，遊泳《墳》、《索》，佩服師言。

translations.literal: Emperor Jingzong's second son Xiufu, third son Zhizhong, fourth son Yanyang, and sixth son Chengmei all possessed a disposition steeped in harmony and centrality, and conduct marked by reverence and caution; they swam in the Fen and Suo and wore the master's words with respect.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jingzong's second son Xiufu, third son Zhizhong, fourth son Yanyang, and sixth son Chengmei all possessed harmonious dispositions and conduct marked by reverence and caution; they studied the classics and honored their teachers' instruction.

sentences.zh: 宜開土宇之封，用申睦族之典。

translations.literal: It is fitting to open territorial enfeoffments and apply the canon of harmonious kin.
translations.idiomatic: It is fitting to grant them territorial enfeoffments and apply the canon of harmonious kin.

sentences.zh: 休復可封梁王，執中可封襄王，言揚可封紀王，成美可封陳王。

translations.literal: Xiufu may be enfeoffed as Prince of Liang, Zhizhong as Prince of Xiang, Yanyang as Prince of Ji, and Chengmei as Prince of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Xiufu is to be created Prince of Liang, Zhizhong Prince of Xiang, Yanyang Prince of Ji, and Chengmei Prince of Chen.

sentences.zh: 宜令有司擇日備禮冊命。」

translations.literal: The responsible offices should choose a day and prepare ritual for the investiture.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices shall choose a day and prepare the ritual investiture.

sentences.zh: 襄王執中，與梁王同時受封。

translations.literal: Prince of Xiang Zhizhong was enfeoffed at the same time as the Prince of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Xiang, Zhizhong, was enfeoffed at the same time as the Prince of Liang.

sentences.zh: 第三男采，樂平郡王。

translations.literal: His third son Cai was Prince of Leping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His third son, Cai, was Prince of Leping.

sentences.zh: 紀王，與襄王同時受封。

translations.literal: The Prince of Ji was enfeoffed at the same time as the Prince of Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Ji received his enfeoffment at the same time as the Prince of Xiang.

sentences.zh: 陳王成美，與紀王言揚同時受封。

translations.literal: Prince of Chen Chengmei was enfeoffed at the same time as Prince of Ji Yanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Chen, Chengmei, was enfeoffed at the same time as Prince of Ji, Yanyang.

sentences.zh: 開成四年十月，詔曰：「古先哲王之有天下也，何嘗不正國本而承天序，建儲貳而主重離？

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the fourth year of Kaicheng an edict stated: When the ancient sage kings possessed All Under Heaven, how did they not rectify the state foundation to inherit Heaven's sequence and establish the heir to preside over the heavy departure?
translations.idiomatic: In October 839 an edict declared: When the ancient sage kings possessed All Under Heaven, how did they not establish the state foundation to inherit Heaven's mandate and name an heir to preside over the realm?

sentences.zh: 朕以寡昧，祗荷丕圖。

translations.literal: I, with my few virtues, received the great design.
translations.idiomatic: I, with my limited virtues, received the great mandate.

sentences.zh: 虔恭寅畏，思固鴻業，慎擇全懿，曠於旬時。

translations.literal: Reverently respectful and cautious, I thought to secure the great enterprise, carefully selecting the wholly excellent over many days.
translations.idiomatic: Reverent and cautious, I sought to secure the great enterprise, carefully selecting the wholly worthy over many days.

sentences.zh: 而卿士獻謀，龜筮告吉，以為少陽虛位，願舉盛儀。

translations.literal: Yet the ministers offered counsel and the tortoise and milfoil reported auspiciousness, saying that the lesser yang position was vacant and they wished to raise the full ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the ministers offered counsel and the oracle reported auspiciousness, saying that the heir's position was vacant and they wished to conduct the full ceremony.

sentences.zh: 列聖垂休，俾合予誌，選賢而立，式表無私。

translations.literal: The successive sages left their blessing, fitting my intent; selecting the worthy to establish shows no partiality.
translations.idiomatic: The successive sages left their blessing, fitting my intent; to select the worthy and establish him shows no partiality.

sentences.zh: 敬宗皇帝第六男陳王成美，天假忠孝，日新道德；

translations.literal: Emperor Jingzong's sixth son, Prince of Chen Chengmei, Heaven lent him loyalty and filial piety and daily renewed his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jingzong's sixth son, Prince of Chen, Chengmei, was endowed by Heaven with loyalty and filial piety and daily renewed his virtue.

sentences.zh: 溫文合雅，謙敬保和。

translations.literal: Warm in culture, combining elegance, humble and respectful, preserving harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Warm in culture and elegant in manner, humble, respectful, and preserving harmony.

sentences.zh: 裕端明之體度，尚《詩》、《書》之辭訓，言皆中禮，行不違仁。

translations.literal: Abundant in dignified clarity of bearing, he honored the teachings of the Odes and Documents; his words all hit the ritual mark and his conduct did not violate benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: Abundant in dignified bearing, he honored the teachings of the Odes and Documents; his words conformed to ritual and his conduct did not violate benevolence.

sentences.zh: 是可以訓考舊章，欽若成命，授之匕鬯，以奉粢盛。

translations.literal: Therefore he may be instructed according to the old statutes, reverently to follow the completed command, receive the ladles and libation cup, and serve the sacrificial grain.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore he may be instructed according to the old statutes, reverently to follow the completed command, receive the ritual vessels, and serve at the ancestral sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 宜回硃邸之榮，俾踐青宮之重，可立為皇太子。

translations.literal: It is fitting to turn back the glory of the vermilion residence and tread the weight of the green palace; he may be established as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: It is fitting to transfer the glory of his princely residence to the weight of the Eastern Palace; he is to be established as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 宜令所司擇日備禮冊命。

translations.literal: The responsible offices should choose a day and prepare ritual for the investiture.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices shall choose a day and prepare the ritual investiture.

sentences.zh: 」自莊恪太子薨，將相大臣洎職言者，拜章面陳凡累月，上遂命立陳王。

translations.literal: From the time Heir Apparent Zhuangke died, chancellors, great ministers, and remonstrance officials submitted memorials in person for many months, and the emperor then ordered the Prince of Chen established.
translations.idiomatic: After Heir Apparent Zhuangke's death, chancellors, great ministers, and remonstrance officials submitted memorials in person for many months, until the emperor ordered the Prince of Chen established.

sentences.zh: 未行冊禮，復降仍舊，其年殂於籓邸。

translations.literal: Before the investiture rites were performed, he was again demoted to his former status; that year he died at his princely residence.
translations.idiomatic: Before the investiture rites were performed, he was again reduced to his former status; that year he died at his princely residence.

sentences.zh: 第十九男儼，宣城郡王。

translations.literal: His nineteenth son Yan was Prince of Xuancheng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His nineteenth son, Yan, was Prince of Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 文宗二子：莊恪太子永、蔣王宗儉。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong had two sons: Heir Apparent Zhuangke Yong and Prince of Jiang Zongjian.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong had two sons: Heir Apparent Zhuangke, Yong, and Prince of Jiang, Zongjian.

sentences.zh: 莊恪太子永，文宗長子也。

translations.literal: Heir Apparent Zhuangke Yong was Emperor Wenzong's eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Heir Apparent Zhuangke, Yong, was Emperor Wenzong's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 母曰王德妃。

translations.literal: His mother was Virtuous Consort Wang.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was Virtuous Consort Wang.

sentences.zh: 太和四年正月，封魯王。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year of Taihe he was enfeoffed as Prince of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of 830 he was created Prince of Lu.

sentences.zh: 六年，上以王年幼，思得賢傅輔導之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the emperor, because the prince was young, wished to obtain worthy tutors to guide him.
translations.idiomatic: In 832 the emperor, finding the prince still young, wished to obtain worthy tutors to guide him.

sentences.zh: 時王傅和元亮，因待制召問。

translations.literal: At that time the prince's tutor He Yuanliang was summoned for consultation as a attendant draftsman.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the prince's tutor He Yuanliang was summoned for consultation in his capacity as attendant draftsman.

sentences.zh: 元亮出於卒吏，不知書，一不能對。

translations.literal: Yuanliang came from the ranks of clerks and knew no books; he could not answer a single question.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanliang had risen from the clerk corps and was illiterate; he could not answer a single question.

sentences.zh: 後宰相延英奏事，上從容曰：「魯王質性可教，宜擇賢士大夫為官屬，不可復用和元亮之輩。

translations.literal: Later when the chancellor reported affairs at the Yanying Hall, the emperor said calmly: The Prince of Lu's nature can be taught; worthy scholar-officials should be chosen as his staff, and men like He Yuanliang must not be used again.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the chancellor reported affairs at the Yanying Hall, the emperor remarked calmly that the Prince of Lu's nature could be cultivated, that worthy scholar-officials should be chosen for his staff, and that men like He Yuanliang must never be used again.

sentences.zh: 」因以戶部侍郎庾敬休守本官，兼魯王傅；

translations.literal: Accordingly Vice Minister of Revenue Yu Jingxiu retained his original office and concurrently served as tutor to the Prince of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jingxiu, vice minister of revenue, was therefore ordered to retain his original office and serve concurrently as tutor to the Prince of Lu.

sentences.zh: 太常卿鄭肅守本官，兼王府長史；

translations.literal: Minister of Rites Zheng Su retained his original office and concurrently served as chief administrator of the princely establishment.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Su, minister of rites, retained his original office and concurrently served as chief administrator of the princely establishment.

sentences.zh: 戶部郎中李踐方守本官，兼王府司馬。

translations.literal: Director in the Ministry of Revenue Li Jianfang retained his original office and concurrently served as marshal of the princely establishment.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jianfang, director in the ministry of revenue, retained his original office and concurrently served as marshal of the princely establishment.

sentences.zh: 其年十月，降詔冊為皇太子。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of that year an edict was issued enfeoffing him as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of that year an edict was issued making him crown prince.

sentences.zh: 開成三年，上以皇太子宴遊敗度，不可教導，將議廢黜。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kaicheng the emperor, because the crown prince's feasting and roaming exceeded proper bounds and he could not be instructed, was about to discuss deposition.
translations.idiomatic: In 838 the emperor, because the crown prince's feasting and roaming exceeded proper bounds and he could not be instructed, was about to discuss deposition.

sentences.zh: 特開延英，召宰臣及兩省御史臺五品已上、南班四品已上官對。

translations.literal: He specially opened the Yanying Hall and summoned chancellors, officials of the two departments and the Censorate of the fifth rank and above, and officials of the southern court of the fourth rank and above to face him.
translations.idiomatic: He specially opened the Yanying Hall and summoned chancellors, officials of the two departments and the Censorate of the fifth rank and above, and officials of the southern court of the fourth rank and above to address them.

sentences.zh: 宰臣及眾官以為儲後年小，可俟改過，國本至重，願寬宥。

translations.literal: The chancellors and all officials said that the heir was young and might wait to reform; the state foundation was supremely important and they begged leniency.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellors and all officials said that the heir was young and might yet reform; the state foundation was supremely important and they begged leniency.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞狄兼謨上前雪涕以諫，詞理懇切。

translations.literal: Censor-in-chief Di Jianmo stepped forward with tears streaming to remonstrate, his reasoning earnest.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Di Jianmo stepped forward in tears to remonstrate, his reasoning earnest and forceful.

sentences.zh: 翌日，翰林學士六人洎神策六軍軍使十六人又進表陳論，上意稍解。

translations.literal: The next day six Hanlin academicians together with sixteen military commissioners of the six Shence armies also submitted memorials arguing the case, and the emperor's intent softened somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: The following day six Hanlin academicians and sixteen military commissioners of the six Shence armies submitted further memorials, and the emperor's resolve softened somewhat.

sentences.zh: 其日一更，太子歸少陽院，以中人張克己、柏常心充少陽院使；

translations.literal: That day at the first watch the crown prince returned to the Shaoyang Residence; the eunuchs Zhang Keji and Bai Changxin were appointed commissioners of the Shaoyang Residence.
translations.idiomatic: That night at the first watch the crown prince returned to the Shaoyang Residence; the eunuchs Zhang Keji and Bai Changxin were appointed commissioners there.

sentences.zh: 如京使王少華、判官袁載和及品官、白身、內園小兒、官人等數十人，連坐至死及剝色、流竄。

translations.literal: Such officials as Capital Envoy Wang Shaohua, adjutant Yuan Zaihe, ranked officials, commoners, inner-garden boys, and palace personnel numbering several tens were implicated and sentenced to death, stripping of rank, or exile.
translations.idiomatic: Several dozen persons implicated with them—including Capital Envoy Wang Shaohua, adjutant Yuan Zaihe, ranked officials, commoners, inner-garden boys, and palace staff—were sentenced to death, stripping of rank, or exile.

sentences.zh: 尋詔侍讀竇宗直、周敬慎依前隔日入少陽院。

translations.literal: Soon an edict ordered reading tutors Dou Zongzhi and Zhou Jingshen to enter the Shaoyang Residence on alternate days as before.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict restored reading tutors Dou Zongzhi and Zhou Jingshen to entering the Shaoyang Residence on alternate days.

sentences.zh: 其年薨，敕兵部尚書王起撰哀冊文曰：

translations.literal: That year he died; an edict ordered Minister of War Wang Qi to compose the lamentation text, which stated:
translations.idiomatic: That year he died; the emperor ordered Minister of War Wang Qi to compose the lamentation, which read:

sentences.zh: 維大唐開成三年，歲次戊午，十月乙酉朔，十六日庚子，皇太子薨於少陽院。

translations.literal: In the great Tang, the third year of Kaicheng, the year wuwu, on the sixteenth day gengzi of the tenth month, with yiyou as the first day of the month, the crown prince died at the Shaoyang Residence.
translations.idiomatic: In the great Tang, the third year of Kaicheng, the year wuwu, on the sixteenth day gengzi of the tenth month, with yiyou as the first day of the month, the crown prince died at the Shaoyang Residence.

sentences.zh: 十七日辛丑，遷座於大吉殿。

translations.literal: On the seventeenth day xinchou his coffin was moved to the Daji Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventeenth day xinchou his coffin was moved to the Daji Hall.

sentences.zh: 十一月乙卯朔，二十四日戊寅，命冊使太子太師兼右僕射、門下侍郎、國子祭酒、平章事鄭覃，副使中書侍郎、平章事楊嗣復，持節冊謚曰莊恪。

translations.literal: On the twenty-fourth day wuyin of the eleventh month, with yimao as the first day, the investiture envoy Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, concurrent Right Vice Director, Gate Department Vice Director, Chancellor of the Directorate of Education, and Grand Councillor Zheng Tan, and deputy envoy Secretariat Vice Director and Grand Councillor Yang Sifu, bearing credentials, invested the posthumous title Zhuangke.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-fourth day wuyin of the eleventh month, with yimao as the first day, the investiture envoy Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, concurrent Right Vice Director, Gate Department Vice Director, Chancellor of the Directorate of Education, and Grand Councillor Zheng Tan, and deputy envoy Secretariat Vice Director and Grand Councillor Yang Sifu, bearing credentials, invested the posthumous title Zhuangke.

sentences.zh: 十二月乙酉朔，十二日丙申，葬於驪山之北原莊恪陵，禮也。

translations.literal: On the twelfth day bingshen of the twelfth month, with yiyou as the first day, he was buried at the northern plain of Mount Li at the Zhuangke tomb, according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: On the twelfth day bingshen of the twelfth month, with yiyou as the first day, he was buried at the northern plain of Mount Li at the Zhuangke tomb, according to ritual.

sentences.zh: 玉琯歲窮，金壺漏盡，祖奠告徹，哀笳將引。

translations.literal: The jade pitch-pipe year reached its end, the golden clepsydra's drip exhausted; the ancestral offering was declared complete and the mourning pipes were about to lead forth.
translations.idiomatic: The year's measure ran its course, the water clock exhausted its drip; the ancestral offering was declared complete and the mourning pipes were about to lead forth.

sentences.zh: 庭滅燎而月寒，路搖旍而風緊。

translations.literal: In the courtyard the torches were extinguished and the moon was cold; along the road the banners swayed and the wind was tight.
translations.idiomatic: In the courtyard the torches were extinguished and the moon was cold; along the road the banners swayed and the wind was tight.

sentences.zh: 皇帝念主鬯之缺位，悼佩觿之夭年。

translations.literal: The emperor, thinking of the vacant position of the chief sacrifice and mourning the heir's early death.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grieved the vacant position of the chief sacrifice and mourned the heir's early death.

sentences.zh: 銅樓已閉，銀牒徒懸。

translations.literal: The bronze tower was already closed; the silver tally hung in vain.
translations.idiomatic: The bronze tower was already closed; the silver tally hung in vain.

sentences.zh: 方追思於對日，遽冥寞而賓天。

translations.literal: Just as he pursued remembrance of facing the sun, suddenly he was dark and silent, a guest of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Just as he pursued remembrance of facing the sun, suddenly he was dark and silent, a guest of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 典冊具舉，文物鹹備。

translations.literal: The statutes and documents were all raised; the cultural objects were all complete.
translations.idiomatic: The statutes and documents were all raised; the cultural objects were all complete.

sentences.zh: 爰詔侍臣，顯揚上嗣，其詞曰：

translations.literal: Therefore he ordered attendant ministers to display and praise the primary heir; the text states:
translations.idiomatic: Therefore he ordered attendant ministers to display and praise the primary heir; the text states:

sentences.zh: 皇矣帝緒，肇基綿古；

translations.literal: Sublime is the imperial line, its foundation laid in remote antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Sublime is the imperial line, its foundation laid in remote antiquity.

sentences.zh: 種德尊道，宗文祖武。

translations.literal: Planting virtue and honoring the Way, he venerates the literary and martial ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: Planting virtue and honoring the Way, he venerates the literary and martial ancestors.

sentences.zh: 上聖開成，天下和平；

translations.literal: The supreme sage opens the Kaicheng era; All Under Heaven is at peace.
translations.idiomatic: The supreme sage opens the Kaicheng era; All Under Heaven is at peace.

sentences.zh: 儲祉發祥，是生元良。

translations.literal: Stored blessings issue auspicious omens; thereby the primary worthy is born.
translations.idiomatic: Stored blessings issue auspicious omens; thereby the primary worthy is born.

sentences.zh: 覃訏之初，岐嶷用彰；

translations.literal: At the beginning of his swaddling, his precocious intelligence was displayed.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of his swaddling, his precocious intelligence was displayed.

sentences.zh: 蘊才遊藝，玉裕金相。

translations.literal: He stored talent and roamed in the arts, jade in abundance and gold in aspect.
translations.idiomatic: He stored talent and cultivated the arts, jade in abundance and gold in aspect.

sentences.zh: 既免孩提，是加封殖；

translations.literal: Once past infancy, enfeoffment was added.
translations.idiomatic: Once past infancy, enfeoffment was added.

sentences.zh: 俾維城於東魯，錫介珪於上國。

translations.literal: He was made a bulwark city in eastern Lu and granted the secondary jade tablet of the upper state.
translations.idiomatic: He was made a bulwark prince in eastern Lu and granted the secondary jade tablet of the upper state.

sentences.zh: 辭榮硃邸，正位青宮；

translations.literal: He declined the glory of the vermilion residence and took the correct position of the green palace.
translations.idiomatic: He declined the glory of the vermilion residence and took the correct position of the green palace.

sentences.zh: 尊師重傅，養德含聰。

translations.literal: Honoring teachers and respecting tutors, he nourished virtue and embraced wisdom.
translations.idiomatic: Honoring teachers and respecting tutors, he nourished virtue and embraced wisdom.

sentences.zh: 畏馳道而不絕，問寢門而益恭。

translations.literal: He feared the imperial roadway yet did not cut it off; he inquired at the bedchamber gate and became still more respectful.
translations.idiomatic: He feared the imperial roadway yet did not cut it off; he inquired at the bedchamber gate and became still more respectful.

sentences.zh: 招賢警戒，齒胄謙沖；

translations.literal: He summoned the worthy with warning and caution; in the school for heirs he was humble and modest.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned the worthy with warning and caution; in the school for heirs he was humble and modest.

sentences.zh: 冀日躋於三善，奉天慈於九重。

translations.literal: He hoped daily to ascend the three excellences and serve Heaven's kindness in the ninefold palace.
translations.idiomatic: He hoped daily to ascend the three excellences and serve Heaven's kindness in the ninefold palace.

sentences.zh: 漢莊好學，既顯於外；

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuang of Han loved learning, which was already manifest outwardly.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuang of Han loved learning, which was already manifest outwardly.

sentences.zh: 魏丕能文，方循於內。

translations.literal: Pi of Wei could compose literature and followed the inner path.
translations.idiomatic: Pi of Wei could compose literature and followed the inner path.

sentences.zh: 美不二於顏過，嘉得三於鯉退。

translations.literal: He did not double the beauty of Yan's fault; he thrice rejoiced at the carp's return.
translations.idiomatic: He did not double the beauty of Yan's fault; he thrice rejoiced at the carp's return.

sentences.zh: 焜耀甲觀，鏗鏘瑜珮。

translations.literal: He shone in the armor of the heir's palace; his jade pendants rang clear.
translations.idiomatic: He shone in the armor of the heir's palace; his jade pendants rang clear.

sentences.zh: 方積善於為山，何反真而遊岱。

translations.literal: Just as he was accumulating goodness like a mountain, how did he reverse truth and roam to Mount Dai?
translations.idiomatic: Just as he was accumulating goodness like a mountain, how did he reverse truth and roam to Mount Dai?

sentences.zh: 嗚呼哀哉！

translations.literal: Alas, how mournful!
translations.idiomatic: Alas, how mournful!

sentences.zh: 憂兢損壽，沈屙始遘；

translations.literal: Anxiety and caution shortened his life; a deep malady first appeared.
translations.idiomatic: Anxiety and caution shortened his life; a deep malady first appeared.

sentences.zh: 群望並走，百靈宜祐。

translations.literal: All who looked on ran together; the hundred spirits should have aided him.
translations.idiomatic: All who looked on ran together; the hundred spirits should have aided him.

sentences.zh: 吳客之問徒為，越人之方靡救。

translations.literal: The Wu physician's inquiry was in vain; the Yue man's prescription could not save him.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu physician's inquiry was in vain; the Yue man's prescription could not save him.

sentences.zh: 占前星之掩曜，知東朝之降咎；

translations.literal: Observing the former star's eclipse, one knew the Eastern Palace's descent into calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Observing the former star's eclipse, one knew the Eastern Palace's descent into calamity.

sentences.zh: 天垂象而則然，人由己而何有？

translations.literal: Heaven hung forth its signs and it was thus; what fault had man in himself?
translations.idiomatic: Heaven hung forth its signs and it was thus; what fault had man in himself?

sentences.zh: 嗚呼哀哉！

translations.literal: Alas, how mournful!
translations.idiomatic: Alas, how mournful!

sentences.zh: 稅駕乘華兮即宮夜臺，鳳笙長絕兮蜃輅徐來。

translations.literal: He rested his carriage and rode the flowering carriage to the palace's night terrace; the phoenix pipes were long cut off and the clam carriage came slowly.
translations.idiomatic: He rested his carriage and entered the palace of the dead; the phoenix pipes fell silent forever and the funeral carriage came slowly.

sentences.zh: 啟青宮而右出，歷玄灞而左回；

translations.literal: Opening the green palace he went out to the right, passing the dark ford he turned left.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving the Eastern Palace to the right, he passed the dark ford and turned left.

sentences.zh: 度雕林兮魂斷，入曠野兮心摧。

translations.literal: Crossing the carved forest his soul was severed; entering the open wilds his heart was shattered.
translations.idiomatic: Passing the carved forest, his spirit was cut off; entering the open wilderness, his heart was broken.

sentences.zh: 水助挽而幽咽，雲帶翣而徘徊；

translations.literal: Water aided the bier and sobbed faintly; clouds bore the plume covers and hovered.
translations.idiomatic: The waters aided the bier in a choked sob; clouds bore the funeral plumes as they drifted.

sentences.zh: 悲佳城之已掩，見新廟之方開。

translations.literal: Grieving that the fine city was already covered, seeing the new temple just opened.
translations.idiomatic: Grieving that the fine tomb was already sealed, seeing the new temple just opened.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼哀哉！

translations.literal: Alas, how mournful!
translations.idiomatic: Alas, how mournful!

sentences.zh: 授經兮曷期，執紼兮增欷；

translations.literal: To transmit the classics—how could the term be known; holding the mourning cord—sighs increased.
translations.idiomatic: To transmit the classics—when could that be hoped for; holding the mourning cord—sighs only increased.

sentences.zh: 九原作兮何嗟及，七日還兮安可希。

translations.literal: At Jiuyuan who could sigh in time; returning in seven days—how could it be hoped for.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiuyuan who could sigh in time; returning in seven days—how could it be hoped for.

sentences.zh: 有少海之波逝，無西園之蓋飛；

translations.literal: There were waves of the lesser sea passing away, but no canopy of the western garden flying.
translations.idiomatic: The lesser sea's waves passed away, but no canopy of the western garden flew.

sentences.zh: 商山之羽翼已散，望苑之賓客鹹歸。

translations.literal: The wings of Mount Shang had already scattered; the guests of Wangyuan all returned.
translations.idiomatic: The wings of Mount Shang had already scattered; the guests of Wangyuan all returned.

sentences.zh: 瑟彼玉簡，閟於泉扉；

translations.literal: Serene are those jade tablets, shut within the spring gate.
translations.idiomatic: Serene are those jade tablets, shut within the tomb gate.

sentences.zh: 用傳信於文字，願不昧於音徽。

translations.literal: Using transmitted faith in written words, may he not be obscured in musical elegance.
translations.idiomatic: May the written words convey his faith, that his fame not be obscured.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼哀哉！

translations.literal: Alas, how mournful!
translations.idiomatic: Alas, how mournful!

sentences.zh: 蔣王宗儉，文宗第二子，開成二年封。

translations.literal: Prince of Jiang Zongjian was Emperor Wenzong's second son; he was enfeoffed in the second year of Kaicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jiang, Zongjian, was Emperor Wenzong's second son; he was enfeoffed in 837.

sentences.zh: 武宗五子：杞王峻，開成五年封；

translations.literal: Emperor Wuzong had five sons: Prince of Qi Jun, enfeoffed in the fifth year of Kaicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wuzong had five sons: Prince of Qi, Jun, enfeoffed in 840.

sentences.zh: 益王峴、兗王岐、德王嶧、昌王嵯，皆會昌二年封。

translations.literal: Prince of Yi Xian, Prince of Yan Qi, Prince of De Yi, and Prince of Chang Cuo were all enfeoffed in the second year of Huichang.
translations.idiomatic: The princes of Yi (Xian), Yan (Qi), De (Yi), and Chang (Cuo) were all enfeoffed in 842.

sentences.zh: 宣宗十一子：懿宗皇帝，余並封王。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong had eleven sons: Emperor Yizong, and the rest were all enfeoffed as princes.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong had eleven sons: Emperor Yizong, and the rest were all created princes.

sentences.zh: 靖懷太子漢，會昌六年封雍王，大中六年薨，冊贈靖懷太子。

translations.literal: Heir Apparent Jinghuai Han was enfeoffed as Prince of Yong in the sixth year of Huichang, died in the sixth year of Dazhong, and was posthumously invested as Heir Apparent Jinghuai.
translations.idiomatic: Heir Apparent Jinghuai, Han, was created Prince of Yong in 846, died in 852, and was posthumously invested as Heir Apparent Jinghuai.

sentences.zh: 雅王涇，宣宗第二子。

translations.literal: Prince of Ya Jing was Emperor Xuanzong's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Ya, Jing, was Emperor Xuanzong's second son.

sentences.zh: 大中元年封。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed in the first year of Dazhong.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed in 847.

sentences.zh: 夔王滋，宣宗第三子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Kui Zi was Emperor Xuanzong's third son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Kui, Zi, was Emperor Xuanzong's third son.

sentences.zh: 會昌六年封，咸通四年薨。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed in the sixth year of Huichang and died in the fourth year of Xiantong.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed in 846 and died in 863.

sentences.zh: 慶王沂，第四子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Qing Yi was the fourth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Qing, Yi, was the fourth son.

sentences.zh: 會昌六年封，大中四十年薨。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed in the sixth year of Huichang and died in the fortieth year of Dazhong.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed in 846 and died in the fourth year of Dazhong.

sentences.zh: 濮王澤，第五子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Pu Ze was the fifth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Pu, Ze, was the fifth son.

sentences.zh: 大中二年封。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed in the second year of Dazhong.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed in 848.

sentences.zh: 鄂王潤，第六子也。

translations.literal: Prince of E Run was the sixth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of E, Run, was the sixth son.

sentences.zh: 大中五年封，乾符三年薨。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed in the fifth year of Dazhong and died in the third year of Qianfu.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed in 851 and died in 876.

sentences.zh: 懷王洽，第七子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Huai Qia was the seventh son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Huai, Qia, was the seventh son.

sentences.zh: 大中八年封。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed in the eighth year of Dazhong.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed in 854.

sentences.zh: 昭王汭，第八子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Zhao Rui was the eighth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Zhao, Rui, was the eighth son.

sentences.zh: 大中八年封，乾符三年薨。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed in the eighth year of Dazhong and died in the third year of Qianfu.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed in 854 and died in 876.

sentences.zh: 康王汶，大中八年封。

translations.literal: Prince of Kang Wen was enfeoffed in the eighth year of Dazhong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Kang, Wen, was enfeoffed in 854.

sentences.zh: 廣王澭，大中十一年封。

translations.literal: Prince of Guang Huang was enfeoffed in the eleventh year of Dazhong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Guang, Huang, was enfeoffed in 857.

sentences.zh: 懿宗八子：僖宗皇帝、昭宗皇帝，余並封王。

translations.literal: Emperor Yizong had eight sons: Emperor Xizong and Emperor Zhaozong, and the rest were all enfeoffed as princes.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yizong had eight sons: the emperors Xizong and Zhaozong, and the rest were all created princes.

sentences.zh: 魏王佾，咸通三年封。

translations.literal: Prince of Wei Ji was enfeoffed in the third year of Xiantong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Wei, Ji, was enfeoffed in 862.

sentences.zh: 涼王健，咸通三年封，乾符六年薨。

translations.literal: Prince of Liang Jian was enfeoffed in the third year of Xiantong and died in the sixth year of Qianfu.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Liang, Jian, was enfeoffed in 862 and died in 879.

sentences.zh: 蜀王佶，咸通三年封。

translations.literal: Prince of Shu Ji was enfeoffed in the third year of Xiantong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Shu, Ji, was enfeoffed in 862.

sentences.zh: 鹹王侃，咸通六年封郢王，十年改封今王。

translations.literal: Prince of Xian Kan was enfeoffed as Prince of Ying in the sixth year of Xiantong and in the tenth year changed to his present princedom.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Xian, Kan, was created Prince of Ying in 865 and in 869 was transferred to his present princedom.

sentences.zh: 吉王保，咸通十三年封，文德元年八月九日授開府儀同三司、檢校太傅，仍加食邑三百戶。

translations.literal: Prince of Ji Bao was enfeoffed in the thirteenth year of Xiantong; on the ninth day of the eighth month of the first year of Wende he was appointed Grand Preceptor with ceremonial honors equal to the Three Excellencies and Acting Grand Tutor, with an additional three hundred households added to his fief.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Ji, Bao, was enfeoffed in 872; on the ninth day of the eighth month of 888 he was appointed Grand Preceptor with honors equal to the Three Excellencies and acting Grand Tutor, with three hundred additional fief households.

sentences.zh: 睦王倚，咸通十三年封。

translations.literal: Prince of Mu Yi was enfeoffed in the thirteenth year of Xiantong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Mu, Yi, was enfeoffed in 872.

sentences.zh: 僖宗二子：

translations.literal: Emperor Xizong had two sons:
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xizong had two sons:

sentences.zh: 建王震，中和元年九月十六日封。

translations.literal: Prince of Jian Zhen was enfeoffed on the sixteenth day of the ninth month of the first year of Zhonghe.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jian, Zhen, was enfeoffed on the sixteenth day of the ninth month of 881.

sentences.zh: 益王升，光啟三年十一月十四日封。

translations.literal: Prince of Yi Sheng was enfeoffed on the fourteenth day of the eleventh month of the third year of Guangqi.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Yi, Sheng, was enfeoffed on the fourteenth day of the eleventh month of 887.

sentences.zh: 昭宗十子：哀帝，余並封王。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhaozong had ten sons: Emperor Ai, and the rest were all enfeoffed as princes.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhaozong had ten sons: Emperor Ai, and the rest were all created princes.

sentences.zh: 德王裕，昭宗長子也。

translations.literal: Prince of De Yu was Emperor Zhaozong's eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of De, Yu, was Emperor Zhaozong's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 大順二年六月二十八日封，乾寧四年二月十四日冊為皇太子。

translations.literal: On the twenty-eighth day of the sixth month of the second year of Dashun he was enfeoffed; on the fourteenth day of the second month of the fourth year of Qianning he was invested as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-eighth day of the sixth month of 891 he was enfeoffed; on the fourteenth day of the second month of 897 he was invested as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 時駕在華州，韓建畏諸王主兵，誘防城卒張行思、花重武相次告通王以下欲殺建。

translations.literal: At that time the imperial carriage was at Hua Prefecture; Han Jian, fearing the princes' command of troops, induced the garrison soldiers Zhang Xingsi and Hua Chongwu in succession to report that from the Prince of Tong downward they wished to kill Jian.
translations.idiomatic: The court was then at Hua Prefecture. Han Jian, fearing that the princes commanded troops, induced garrison soldiers Zhang Xingsi and Hua Chongwu in turn to report that the Prince of Tong and those below him intended to kill Jian.

sentences.zh: 建他日又造訛言云：諸王欲劫遷車駕，別幸籓鎮。

translations.literal: On another day Jian also fabricated slanderous words saying the princes wished to seize the imperial carriage and remove it to a border commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On another day Jian also fabricated slander saying the princes wished to seize the imperial carriage and remove it to a border commandery.

sentences.zh: 諸王懼，詣建自陳。

translations.literal: The princes were afraid and went to Jian to explain themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The princes were afraid and went to Jian to explain themselves.

sentences.zh: 建乃延入臥內，密遣人奏云：「今日睦王、濟王、韶王、通王、彭王、韓王、儀王、陳王等八人到臣理所，不測事由。

translations.literal: Jian then invited them into his sleeping quarters and secretly sent someone to memorialize: Today the Princes of Mu, Ji, Shao, Tong, Peng, Han, Yi, and Chen, eight in all, came to my office for reasons I cannot fathom.
translations.idiomatic: Jian invited them into his private quarters and secretly reported: Today the Princes of Mu, Ji, Shao, Tong, Peng, Han, Yi, and Chen—eight in all—came to my office for reasons I cannot discern.

sentences.zh: 臣竊量事體，不合與諸王相見，兼恐久在臣所，於事非宜。

translations.literal: I privately measure the situation and think it improper to meet with the princes; I also fear that keeping them long at my office would be disadvantageous to affairs.
translations.idiomatic: I privately measure the situation and think it improper to meet with the princes; I also fear that keeping them long at my office would be disadvantageous to affairs.

sentences.zh: 忽然及門，意不可測。

translations.literal: Suddenly arriving at my door—their intent cannot be measured.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly arriving at my door—their intent cannot be measured.

sentences.zh: 」又上疏抗請歸十六宅。

translations.literal: He also submitted a memorial firmly requesting that they return to the Sixteen Mansions.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted a memorial firmly requesting that they return to the Sixteen Mansions.

sentences.zh: 如是者數四，帝不允。

translations.literal: Thus four times; the emperor did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: He did this four times; the emperor did not consent.

sentences.zh: 建懼為諸王所圖，乃以精甲數千圍行宮，請誅定州護駕軍都將李筠。

translations.literal: Jian, fearing the princes would plot against him, surrounded the traveling palace with several thousand elite armored troops and requested execution of Li Yun, commander of the Dingzhou army protecting the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Jian, fearing the princes would plot against him, surrounded the traveling palace with several thousand elite armored troops and requested execution of Li Yun, commander of the Dingzhou army protecting the carriage.

sentences.zh: 帝懼甚，詔斬筠於大雲橋。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly afraid and ordered Yun beheaded at the Dayun Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly afraid and ordered Yun beheaded at the Dayun Bridge.

sentences.zh: 其三都軍士，尋放還本道。

translations.literal: The soldiers of the three metropolitan armies were soon released to return to their original circuits.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers of the three metropolitan armies were soon released to return to their original circuits.

sentences.zh: 殿後都，亦與三都元繞行宮扈蹕。

translations.literal: The rear-guard command also, together with the three metropolitan armies, originally escorted the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: The rear-guard command also, together with the three metropolitan armies, originally escorted the traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 至昌，並急詔散之。

translations.literal: By the time they reached Chang, urgent edicts had dispersed them all.
translations.idiomatic: By the time they reached Chang, urgent edicts had dispersed them all.

sentences.zh: 罷諸王兵柄。

translations.literal: The princes' military authority was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The princes' military authority was abolished.

sentences.zh: 建慮上不悅，乃上表請立德王為皇太子。

translations.literal: Jian, concerned the emperor was displeased, then submitted a memorial requesting that the Prince of De be established as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Jian, concerned the emperor was displeased, then submitted a memorial requesting that the Prince of De be established as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 其年八月，嗣延王戒丕自太原還，詔與通王已下八王並賜死於石堤谷。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of that year, when Heir Apparent Yan Jiepi returned from Taiyuan, an edict ordered him together with the Prince of Tong and the eight princes below to be granted death at Shidi Valley.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of that year, when Heir Apparent Yan Jiepi returned from Taiyuan, an edict commanded that he, together with the Prince of Tong and the eight princes below, be put to death at Shidi Valley.

sentences.zh: 光化末，樞密使劉季述、王仲先等幽昭宗於東門，冊裕為帝。

translations.literal: At the end of the Guanghua era, Military Affairs Commissioners Liu Jishu and Wang Zhongxian and others imprisoned Emperor Zhaozong at the eastern gate and invested Yu as emperor.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Guanghua era, Military Affairs Commissioners Liu Jishu and Wang Zhongxian and others imprisoned Emperor Zhaozong at the eastern gate and invested Yu as emperor.

sentences.zh: 及天復初誅季述、仲先，與寺人藏於右軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianfu era, when Jishu and Zhongxian were executed, they hid with the temple personnel in the Right Army.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tianfu era, when Jishu and Zhongxian were executed, they hid with the temple personnel in the Right Army.

sentences.zh: 群臣請殺之，昭宗曰：「太子沖幼，為賊輩所立。

translations.literal: The ministers requested they be killed; Emperor Zhaozong said: The crown prince is young and innocent; he was established by the villainous faction.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers requested they be killed; Emperor Zhaozong said: The crown prince is young and innocent; he was established by the villainous faction.

sentences.zh: 」依舊令歸少陽院。

translations.literal: He was ordered as before to return to the Shaoyang Residence.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered as before to return to the Shaoyang Residence.

sentences.zh: 及硃全忠自鳳翔迎駕還京，以德王眉目疏秀，春秋漸盛，常惡之。

translations.literal: When Zhu Quanzhong came from Fengxiang to welcome the carriage back to the capital, because the Prince of De had refined features and was gradually reaching maturity, he constantly hated him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Quanzhong came from Fengxiang to welcome the court back to the capital, because the Prince of De had refined features and was gradually reaching maturity, he constantly hated him.

sentences.zh: 謂崔胤曰：「德王曾竊居寶位，天下知之。

translations.literal: He said to Cui Yin: The Prince of De once usurped the imperial position; all the realm knows it.
translations.idiomatic: He said to Cui Yin: The Prince of De once usurped the imperial position; all the realm knows it.

sentences.zh: 大義滅親，何得久留？

translations.literal: In great righteousness one destroys kin—how can he be kept long?
translations.idiomatic: In great righteousness one destroys kin—how can he be kept long?

sentences.zh: 是教後代以不孝也。

translations.literal: This would teach later generations to be unfilial.
