translations.idiomatic: This would teach later generations to be unfilial.

sentences.zh: 請公密啟。

translations.literal: Please, sir, secretly report this to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Please, sir, secretly report this to the throne.

sentences.zh: 」胤然之，昭宗不納。

translations.literal: Yin agreed, but Emperor Zhaozong did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Yin agreed, but Emperor Zhaozong did not accept it.

sentences.zh: 他日言於全忠，全忠曰：「此國家大事，臣安敢竊議？

translations.literal: On another day he spoke to Quanzhong; Quanzhong said: This is a great affair of state—how dare I privately discuss it?
translations.idiomatic: On another day he spoke to Quanzhong; Quanzhong said: This is a great affair of state—how dare I privately discuss it?

sentences.zh: 乃崔胤賣臣也。

translations.literal: It is Cui Yin who is selling me out.
translations.idiomatic: It is Cui Yin who is selling me out.

sentences.zh: 」尋以哀帝為天下兵馬元帥。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Emperor Ai was made commander-in-chief of all military forces under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Emperor Ai was made commander-in-chief of all military forces under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 後昭宗至洛下，一日幸福先寺，謂樞密使蔣玄暉曰：「德王，朕之愛子，全忠何故須令廢之，又欲殺之？

translations.literal: Later when Emperor Zhaozong reached Luoyang, one day at Xingfu Temple he said to Military Affairs Commissioner Jiang Xuanyun: The Prince of De is my beloved son—why does Quanzhong insist on deposing him and moreover wish to kill him?
translations.idiomatic: Later when Emperor Zhaozong reached Luoyang, one day at Xingfu Temple he said to Military Affairs Commissioner Jiang Xuanyun: The Prince of De is my beloved son—why does Quanzhong insist on deposing him and moreover wish to kill him?

sentences.zh: 」言訖淚下，因嚙其中指血流。

translations.literal: When he finished speaking tears fell; he bit his middle finger until blood flowed.
translations.idiomatic: When he finished speaking tears fell; he bit his middle finger until blood flowed.

sentences.zh: 玄暉具報全忠，由是轉恚。

translations.literal: Xuanyun reported fully to Quanzhong, and for this Quanzhong's rage increased.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanyun reported fully to Quanzhong, and for this Quanzhong's rage increased.

sentences.zh: 昭宗遇弒之日，蔣玄暉於西內置社筵；

translations.literal: On the day Emperor Zhaozong met assassination, Jiang Xuanyun set a community feast in the western inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Emperor Zhaozong met assassination, Jiang Xuanyun set a community feast in the western inner palace.

sentences.zh: 酒酣，德王已下六王皆為玄暉所殺，投屍九曲池。

translations.literal: When the wine was deep, the Prince of De and five princes below were all killed by Xuanyun and their corpses cast into the Nine-Bend Pool.
translations.idiomatic: When the wine had gone deep, Xuanyun killed the Prince of De and five younger princes and cast their bodies into the Nine-Bend Pool.

sentences.zh: 棣王祤。

translations.literal: Prince of Di Mao.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Di, Mao.

sentences.zh: 乾寧元年十月八日封。

translations.literal: Enfeoffed on the eighth day of the tenth month of the first year of Qianning.
translations.idiomatic: Enfeoffed on the eighth day of the tenth month of 894.

sentences.zh: 虔王禊、沂王禋、遂王祎，並與棣王同時封冊。

translations.literal: Prince of Qian Qi, Prince of Yi Yin, and Prince of Sui Yi were all enfeoffed and invested at the same time as the Prince of Di.
translations.idiomatic: The princes of Qian (Qi), Yi (Yin), and Sui (Yi) were all enfeoffed and invested at the same time as the Prince of Di.

sentences.zh: 景王秘，乾寧四年十月二十二日封。

translations.literal: Prince of Jing Mi was enfeoffed on the twenty-second day of the tenth month of the fourth year of Qianning.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jing, Mi, was enfeoffed on the twenty-second day of the tenth month of 897.

sentences.zh: 祁王祺與景王同時封冊。

translations.literal: Prince of Qi Qi was enfeoffed and invested at the same time as the Prince of Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Qi, Qi, was enfeoffed and invested at the same time as the Prince of Jing.

sentences.zh: 雅王禛、瓊王祥，並光化元年十一月九日封。

translations.literal: Prince of Ya Zhen and Prince of Qiong Xiang were both enfeoffed on the ninth day of the eleventh month of the first year of Guanghua.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Ya, Zhen, and Prince of Qiong, Xiang, were both enfeoffed on the ninth day of the eleventh month of 898.

sentences.zh: 嗣襄王襜，性柔善，無他能。

translations.literal: Heir Apparent Xiang Chan was gentle and good by nature and had no other ability.
translations.idiomatic: Heir Apparent Xiang, Chan, was gentle and good by nature and had no other ability.

sentences.zh: 光啟二年春，車駕在寶雞，西軍逼請幸岐隴；

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year of Guangqi the imperial carriage was at Baoji; the western army pressed to request that the court proceed to Qilong.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year of Guangqi the court was at Baoji; the western army pressed to request that the court proceed to Qilong.

sentences.zh: 帝以數十騎自大散關幸興元。

translations.literal: The emperor with several dozen horsemen proceeded from the Great Scatter Pass to Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor with several dozen horsemen proceeded from the Great Scatter Pass to Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 時襜有疾，不能從，因為硃玫所挾至鳳翔。

translations.literal: At that time Chan was ill and could not follow; he was therefore seized by Zhu Mei and taken to Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Chan was ill and could not follow; he was therefore seized by Zhu Mei and taken to Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 有臺省官從行未及者僅百人。

translations.literal: Officials of the Secretariat and Censorate who had not yet caught up numbered barely a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of the Secretariat and Censorate who had not yet caught up numbered barely a hundred.

sentences.zh: 四月，玫乃與宰相蕭遘、裴澈率群僚冊襜為監國。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Mei then together with chancellors Xiao Xun and Pei Che led the mass of officials to invest Chan as regent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Mei joined chancellors Xiao Xun and Pei Che in leading the officials to invest Chan as regent.

sentences.zh: 襜以鄭昌圖判度支，而鹽鐵、戶部各置副使，三司之事，一以委焉，目曰「廢置相公」。

translations.literal: Chan appointed Zheng Changtu to manage the budget, while Salt and Iron and Revenue each had deputy commissioners; affairs of the three offices were all entrusted to him, called the dismissed chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Chan appointed Zheng Changtu to manage the budget, while Salt and Iron and Revenue each had deputy commissioners; affairs of the three offices were all entrusted to him, called the dismissed chancellor.

sentences.zh: 五月，襜遣偽戶部侍郎柳陟等十余人，分諭關東、河北諸道，納偽命者甚眾。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Chan dispatched the bogus Vice Minister of Revenue Liu Zhi and more than ten others to instruct the circuits east of the passes and in Hebei; very many accepted the bogus commands.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Chan dispatched the bogus Vice Minister of Revenue Liu Zhi and more than ten others to instruct the circuits east of the passes and in Hebei; very many accepted the bogus commands.

sentences.zh: 十月，硃玫率蕭遘等冊襜為帝，改元曰永貞，遙尊僖宗為太上元皇聖帝。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Zhu Mei led Xiao Xun and others to invest Chan as emperor, changing the era name to Yongzhen and honoring Emperor Xizong from afar as the Supreme Primordial Sage Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Zhu Mei led Xiao Xun and others to invest Chan as emperor, changing the era name to Yongzhen and honoring Emperor Xizong from afar as the Supreme Primordial Sage Emperor.

sentences.zh: 初，河中王重榮表率東諸侯進貢，唯蔡賊與太原不順。

translations.literal: Initially Wang Chongrong of Hezhong led the eastern feudatories in presenting tribute; only the Cai rebel and Taiyuan did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Initially Wang Chongrong of Hezhong led the eastern feudatories in presenting tribute; only the Cai rebel and Taiyuan did not comply.

sentences.zh: 秦宗權自僭號，太原不協於硃玫故也。

translations.literal: Qin Zongquan had usurped the title; Taiyuan did not cooperate with Zhu Mei for this reason.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Zongquan had usurped the title; Taiyuan did not cooperate with Zhu Mei for this reason.

sentences.zh: 及王行瑜殺硃玫，襜奔至渭上，王重榮使人迎之，襜與偽百官泣別，謂曰：「朕見重榮，當令與卿等各備所服以接卿。

translations.literal: When Wang Xingyu killed Zhu Mei, Chan fled to the Wei River; Wang Chongrong sent men to welcome him; Chan with the bogus hundred officials wept in parting and said: When I see Chongrong I shall have him prepare your respective robes to receive you.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Xingyu killed Zhu Mei, Chan fled to the Wei River; Wang Chongrong sent men to welcome him; Chan with the bogus hundred officials wept in parting and said: When I see Chongrong I shall have him prepare your respective robes to receive you.

sentences.zh: 」殺硃玫之翌日，襜為鄜州亂軍所殺，行瑜遂函首送行在。

translations.literal: The day after Mei was killed, Chan was killed by mutinous troops of Zheng Prefecture; Xingyu then sent the head in a box to the traveling court.
translations.idiomatic: The day after Mei was killed, Chan was killed by mutinous troops of Zheng Prefecture; Xingyu then sent the head in a box to the traveling court.

sentences.zh: 襜四月監國，至十二月死，凡在偽位九月矣。

translations.literal: Chan was regent from the fourth month to death in the twelfth month; altogether he was on the bogus throne nine months.
translations.idiomatic: Chan was regent from April until his death in December; altogether he held the bogus throne nine months.

sentences.zh: 硃玫者，邠州人也。

translations.literal: Zhu Mei was a man of Bin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Mei was a native of Bin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少從邊，以功歷郡守。

translations.literal: In youth he followed the frontier and through merit rose to commandery governor.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he served on the frontier and through merit rose to commandery governor.

sentences.zh: 乾符末，領邠寧節制。

translations.literal: At the end of Qianfu he held the Bingning military commission.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Qianfu era he held the Bingning military commission.

sentences.zh: 中和中，收復京師，與太原李克用、東方達同制加使相。

translations.literal: During Zhonghe he recovered the capital together with Li Keyong of Taiyuan and Dongfang Da, and all three were concurrently promoted to military commissioner and chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhonghe era he recovered the capital together with Li Keyong of Taiyuan and Dongfang Da, and all three were concurrently promoted to military commissioner and chancellor.

sentences.zh: 光啟元年冬，受詔招討河中，軍敗。

translations.literal: In the winter of the first year of Guangqi he received orders to campaign against Hezhong and the army was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of 887 he received orders to campaign against Hezhong and the army was defeated.

sentences.zh: 以軍容使田令孜失策，時諸軍皆怒，乃徇人情，表請誅令孜。

translations.literal: Because Army Affairs Commissioner Tian Lingzi's strategy failed, at that time all armies were angry; he therefore followed popular sentiment and memorialized requesting Lingzi's execution.
translations.idiomatic: Because Army Affairs Commissioner Tian Lingzi's strategy failed, all the armies were angry; he therefore followed popular sentiment and memorialized requesting Lingzi's execution.

sentences.zh: 令孜與楊復恭挾帝西幸，玫又失策。

translations.literal: Lingzi together with Yang Fugong seized the emperor on a western progress, and Mei again failed in strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzi together with Yang Fugong seized the emperor on a western progress, and Mei again failed in strategy.

sentences.zh: 乃虜嗣襄王襜，與蕭遘等同立為帝，大行封拜，以啖諸侯；

translations.literal: He then captured Heir Apparent Xiang Chan and together with Xiao Xun and others established him as emperor, conducting widespread enfeoffments to feed the feudatories.
translations.idiomatic: He then captured Heir Apparent Xiang Chan and together with Xiao Xun and others established him as emperor, conducting widespread enfeoffments to feed the feudatories.

sentences.zh: 而天下之人，歸者十五六焉。

translations.literal: Yet of the people under Heaven, only fifteen or sixteen parts submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Yet of the people under Heaven, only fifteen or sixteen parts submitted.

sentences.zh: 與李昌符始謀冊立，及後，玫自稱大丞相，吐握在己。

translations.literal: He had initially plotted the investiture with Li Changfu, but afterward Mei styled himself Grand Chancellor and held spitting and grasping in his own hands.
translations.idiomatic: He had initially plotted the investiture with Li Changfu, but afterward Mei styled himself Grand Chancellor and held all power in his own hands.

sentences.zh: 昌符怒之。

translations.literal: Changfu was angry at this.
translations.idiomatic: Changfu was angry at this.

sentences.zh: 乃以表送款行在，復密結樞密使楊復恭，人心乃離。

translations.literal: He then sent a memorial of submission to the traveling court and secretly allied with Military Affairs Commissioner Yang Fugong; popular sentiment then turned away.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent a memorial of submission to the traveling court and secretly allied with Military Affairs Commissioner Yang Fugong; popular sentiment then turned away.

sentences.zh: 時行在出令，有能斬硃玫首者，則授以邠帥。

translations.literal: At that time the traveling court issued an order: whoever could cut off Zhu Mei's head would be appointed military commissioner of Bin.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the traveling court issued an order: whoever could cut off Zhu Mei's head would be appointed military commissioner of Bin.

sentences.zh: 賊將王行瑜以大唐峰不利，退保鳳州。

translations.literal: The rebel general Wang Xingyu, finding Datang Peak unfavorable, retreated to defend Feng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel general Wang Xingyu, finding Datang Peak unfavorable, retreated to defend Feng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 終慮得罪，與腹心密謀，徑入京師。

translations.literal: Finally fearing punishment, he conspired secretly with his intimates and went straight into the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Finally fearing punishment, he conspired secretly with his intimates and went straight into the capital.

sentences.zh: 時玫有第在和善裏，行瑜率兵仗入見。

translations.literal: At that time Mei had a mansion in Heshan Ward; Xingyu led armed troops in to see him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Mei had a mansion in Heshan Ward; Xingyu led armed troops in to see him.

sentences.zh: 玫猶責以擅還，行瑜曰：「我要代爾領邠州節制，何復多言？

translations.literal: Mei still reproached him for returning without authorization; Xingyu said: I want to take your place as military commissioner of Bin—why more words?
translations.idiomatic: Mei still rebuked him for returning without leave; Xingyu replied: I mean to take your place as military commissioner of Bin—why speak further?

sentences.zh: 」遂斬之。

translations.literal: He then beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: He then beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 王行瑜者，邠州人也。

translations.literal: Wang Xingyu was a man of Bin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xingyu was a native of Bin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少隸本軍，事硃玫為偏將，平巢寇有功。

translations.literal: In youth he served in the native army, followed Zhu Mei as a subordinate general, and had merit in pacifying the Huang Chao bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he served in the native army, followed Zhu Mei as a subordinate general, and had merit in pacifying the Huang Chao bandits.

sentences.zh: 光啟二年，玫冊嗣襄王襜為偽帝，授天平軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangqi, when Mei invested Heir Apparent Xiang Chan as bogus emperor, he was appointed military commissioner of Tianping.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Guangqi, when Mei invested Heir Apparent Xiang Chan as bogus emperor, he was appointed military commissioner of Tianping.

sentences.zh: 領兵守大散關，攻大唐峰，為李鋌所敗，乃送款行在。

translations.literal: He led troops to guard the Great Scatter Pass and attacked Datang Peak, was defeated by Li Chang, and then sent submission to the traveling court.
translations.idiomatic: He led troops to guard the Great Scatter Pass and attacked Datang Peak, was defeated by Li Chang, and then sent submission to the traveling court.

sentences.zh: 以部下反攻硃玫於闕下，斬之，因授邠州節度使。

translations.literal: With his subordinates he counterattacked Zhu Mei below the palace gates, beheaded him, and was therefore appointed military commissioner of Bin.
translations.idiomatic: With his subordinates he counterattacked Zhu Mei below the palace gates, beheaded him, and was therefore appointed military commissioner of Bin.

sentences.zh: 後平楊守亮於山南，以功累加至中書令。

translations.literal: Later he pacified Yang Shouliang in Shannan and through merit was repeatedly promoted to Secretariat Director.
translations.idiomatic: Later he pacified Yang Shouliang in Shannan and through merit was repeatedly promoted to Secretariat Director.

sentences.zh: 景福中，逼朝廷加尚書令。

translations.literal: During Jingfu he pressed the court to add Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingfu era he pressed the court to add Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 宰臣韋昭度密奏不可。

translations.literal: Chancellor Wei Zhaodu secretly memorialized that this could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Wei Zhaodu secretly memorialized that this could not be done.

sentences.zh: 會韓建、李茂貞稱兵入覲，欲行廢立。

translations.literal: When Han Jian and Li Maozhen raised troops and entered court to pay homage, they wished to carry out deposition and establishment.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Jian and Li Maozhen raised troops and entered court to pay homage, they wished to carry out deposition and establishment.

sentences.zh: 不果，乃請殺昭度與李磎。

translations.literal: It did not succeed; they then requested execution of Zhaodu and Li Xi.
translations.idiomatic: It did not succeed; they then requested execution of Zhaodu and Li Xi.

sentences.zh: 是歲，又遣弟行約攻河中；

translations.literal: That year he also sent his younger brother Xingyue to attack Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: That year he also sent his younger brother Xingyue to attack Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 河中引太原軍至，由是大敗。

translations.literal: Hezhong brought the Taiyuan army; thereby he suffered great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Hezhong brought the Taiyuan army; thereby he suffered great defeat.

sentences.zh: 行約、行實劫駕不獲，遂歸邠州。

translations.literal: Xingyue and Xingshi seized the carriage but did not succeed, and then returned to Bin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xingyue and Xingshi seized the carriage but did not succeed, and then returned to Bin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 行瑜率兵屯梨園，王師圍急。

translations.literal: Xingyu led troops stationed at Liyuan; the imperial army besieged him urgently.
translations.idiomatic: Xingyu led troops stationed at Liyuan; the imperial army besieged him urgently.

sentences.zh: 行實、行約先敗，次保龍泉。

translations.literal: Xingshi and Xingyue were defeated first, then held Longquan.
translations.idiomatic: Xingshi and Xingyue were defeated first, then held Longquan.

sentences.zh: 行瑜又遁至邠州，不能守。

translations.literal: Xingyu again fled to Bin Prefecture and could not hold it.
translations.idiomatic: Xingyu again fled to Bin Prefecture and could not hold it.

sentences.zh: 乾寧二年十一月，挈族至慶州，為部下所殺。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the second year of Qianning he took his clan to Qing Prefecture and was killed by his subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: In November 895 he took his clan to Qing Prefecture and was killed by his subordinates.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：自天寶已降，內官握禁旋，中闈纂繼，皆出其心。

translations.literal: The historian states: From the Tianbao era downward, inner officials grasped the forbidden rotation and succession within the inner quarters—all issued from their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: From the Tianbao reign onward, inner officials controlled the palace guard and succession within the inner quarters—all at their bidding.

sentences.zh: 故手才攬於萬機，目己睨於六宅；

translations.literal: Therefore with their hands they seized the myriad affairs and with their eyes they glared at the Six Mansions.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore with their hands they seized the myriad affairs and with their eyes they glared at the Six Mansions.

sentences.zh: 防閑禁錮，不近人情。

translations.literal: Preventive restraint and imprisonment did not approach human feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Preventive restraint and imprisonment did not approach human feeling.

sentences.zh: 文守好古睦親，至敦友悌。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen loved antiquity and cherished kin, reaching the utmost in fraternal affection.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong loved antiquity and cherished kin, reaching the utmost in fraternal affection.

sentences.zh: 悔前非於齊湊，褒以儲闈；

translations.literal: He regretted his former error toward Qi Cou and praised him with the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He regretted his former error toward Qi Cou and praised him with the Eastern Palace title.

sentences.zh: 付後事於陳王，歸其胄席。

translations.literal: He entrusted later affairs to the Prince of Chen and restored his heir's seat.
translations.idiomatic: He entrusted later affairs to the Prince of Chen and restored his heir's seat.

sentences.zh: 或降輿硃邸，對食瓊筵，怡怡申肺腑之情，穆穆盡棣華之義；

translations.literal: Sometimes he lowered his carriage to the vermilion residence and shared a jade feast, harmoniously expressing feelings of heart and lungs, solemnly fulfilling the righteousness of catalpa blossoms.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes he visited the vermilion residence and shared a feast of jade dishes, expressing kinship with easy warmth and fulfilling fraternal duty with solemn grace.

sentences.zh: 近朝盛美，可洽風謠。

translations.literal: The recent dynasty's flourishing beauty could accord with popular song.
translations.idiomatic: The recent dynasty's flourishing beauty could accord with popular song.

sentences.zh: 昭肅惑讒，毒流安邸。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhaosu was deluded by slander and poison flowed to the Prince of An's residence.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wuzong was deluded by slander and poison flowed to the Prince of An's residence.

sentences.zh: 雖覽大臣之議，欲使磐維；

translations.literal: Although he reviewed the great ministers' counsel and wished to make bedrock secure.
translations.idiomatic: Although he reviewed the great ministers' counsel and wished to make bedrock secure.

sentences.zh: 竟無出閣之儀，終身幽枉。

translations.literal: In the end there was no ceremony of leaving the residence; he was wronged in seclusion for life.
translations.idiomatic: In the end there was no ceremony of leaving the residence; he was wronged in seclusion for life.

sentences.zh: 《谷風》之怨，可為傷心。

translations.literal: The resentment of the Gu Feng—one may grieve at heart.
translations.idiomatic: The grievance voiced in the Gu Feng ode is enough to break the heart.

sentences.zh: 大中、咸通已來，寶圖世及。

translations.literal: From Dazhong and Xiantong onward, the precious design passed from generation to generation.
translations.idiomatic: From the Dazhong and Xiantong eras onward, the imperial succession passed from generation to generation.

sentences.zh: 犬牙麟趾，雖不迨於姬周；

translations.literal: Dog-teeth and phoenix-toes, though not reaching the Zhou of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Dog-teeth and phoenix-toes, though not reaching the Zhou of Ji.

sentences.zh: 平什布謠，未甚悲於宗籍。

translations.literal: The Ping Shi Bu ballad did not greatly grieve the imperial clan registers.
translations.idiomatic: The Ping Shi Bu ballad did not greatly grieve the imperial clan registers.

sentences.zh: 於姬不足，比魏有余。

translations.literal: Falling short of Ji, yet compared with Wei there was surplus.
translations.idiomatic: Falling short of Ji, yet compared with Wei there was surplus.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：周封子弟，運祚綿長。

translations.literal: The encomium states: Zhou enfeoffed sons and younger brothers, and fortune was long-lasting.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium states: Zhou enfeoffed sons and younger brothers, and fortune was long-lasting.

sentences.zh: 管、蔡剿絕，魯、魏克昌。

translations.literal: Guan and Cai were exterminated; Lu and Wei flourished.
translations.idiomatic: Guan and Cai were exterminated; Lu and Wei flourished.

sentences.zh: 誅叛賞順，王者大綱。

translations.literal: Punishing rebellion and rewarding compliance—this is the great outline of kings.
translations.idiomatic: Punishing rebellion and rewarding compliance—this is the great outline of kings.

sentences.zh: 法不私親，棣萼其芳。

translations.literal: Law does not favor kin privately; catalpa and calyx remain fragrant.
translations.idiomatic: Law does not favor kin privately; catalpa and calyx remain fragrant.
